value: floral monoterpene emission is diurnal under a 16 h light / 8 h dark cycle (rises 04:00 to 10:00, peaks 10:00 to 16:00, undetectable at midnight); the daily cycle persists under constant light, with peaks declining gradually from D+6 to D+8; under constant dark emission decreases significantly (a minor peak about one tenth of the constant-light level at 10:00 to 16:00 on D+5, then shifting to 04:00 to 10:00 on D+6 and to midnight on D+7 and D+8)
method: headspace collection of floral monoterpenes at four windows a day (04:00-09:00, 10:00-16:00, 16:00-21:00, 22:00-04:00) from D+4 to D+8; six plants given 16 h/8 h light/dark, then split into constant-light and constant-dark groups
conditions: Phalaenopsis violacea only (P. bellina and two cultivars were used for gene and wavelength work, not for this rhythm test); triplicate biological replicates; authors conclude the rhythm is controlled mainly by the circadian clock and to a lesser degree by light; the short-day condition (8 h/16 h) reduced emission; the circadian conclusion rests on few plants and one photoperiod sequence
